Site handover26-Mar-2026

Scope: sports grounds (padel, basketball and football), a service and toilet building, landscape works, bike and walking paths, and parking at three sites in Asir, Jazan and Jeddah.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. The project is at 55.4% against 67.2% planned, 11.8% behind (SPI 0.82). It gained 4.5% this week against 3.0% planned, so the gap narrowed from 13.3% on 16-Nov-2026. More than half of the gain is procurement (+2.6% of the project), because the schedule update closed 61 procurement activities, most of them with actual dates months in the past. Jazan gained 3.5% of its own scope, Asir 3.3% and Jeddah 0.8%; Jazan is still furthest behind at 40.7% against 61.3% planned.

Project completion is forecast 105 days late. The P6 update and the report summary (data date 23-Nov-2026) forecast completion on 10-May-2027, 29 days earlier than on 16-Nov-2026 but still 105 days after the contract completion date of 25-Jan-2027; the Milestones sheet still gives 08-Jun-2027. P6 shows −86 days of float on project completion and 164 open activities with negative float. The recovery comes from the update itself, not from site output: it closed 91 activities, 79 of them with actual finish dates before the previous data date, including the air dome material approvals that last week's update showed as not started. The critical path now runs through Jazan: fabrication and delivery of the air dome emergency doors (24-Nov to 22-Dec-2026), then the football and padel court surfaces, sports equipment and the padel fence.

Work reported this weekThe works-done files (15 and 16) repeat last week's text word for word, without quantities: court slabs cast in Asir; air dome foundations finished and glass-front steelwork under way; irrigation pipes laid in Asir and Jeddah; tiling, facade stone and roof waterproofing of the toilets; light-pole trenching and cables at all sites; walkway backfilling; and the Jazan water tank cast. The photos show walkway preparation and irrigation in Jeddah, planting curbs in Jazan and Asir, and air dome materials and interlock delivered.
No quantity moved this weekEvery finished quantity in the Major Quantities sheet is the same as on 16-Nov-2026. Behind the plan to date: earthworks at 57,000 of 60,000 m³ planned, sewer and drainage pipe at 55 of 177 LM, 150 mm uPVC pipe at 50 of 150 m, irrigation pipe at 4,000 of 5,000 m and lighting poles at 120 of 180. Hardscape, trees, the air dome, site furniture, ceramic tiles and lighting fixtures are still at 0, although tiling is reported under way and the Procurement Log shows all 322 poles and 129 interior light fittings delivered.

Levelling works are marked complete on 13-Oct-2026 in the weekly report, while P6 still shows the milestone open, now forecast for 24-Nov-2026. * The testing and commissioning baseline of 29-Apr-2026 is as given in the Milestones sheet and appears to be wrong.

Data notes

  • The P6 update UPS-30 closed 91 activities that were open in UPS-29: 61 procurement, 15 engineering and 15 construction. 79 of them carry actual finish dates before the previous data date of 16-Nov-2026 (for example the air dome PVC membrane and steel tension cable approvals, dated April and May 2026, which UPS-29 showed as not started) and 3 carry actual finish dates after the 23-Nov-2026 data date (Asir distribution panels 10-Dec, Asir exhaust ducts 06-Dec, Jazan package units 03-Dec-2026). This drives most of the week's procurement gain and the 29-day recovery of the forecast finish; the back-dated progress should be confirmed by the consultant.
  • Budgeted man-hours in this week's Weekly Progress Report, Progress and Physical-Chart Data sheets are one tenth of last week's (total 40,625.5 instead of 406,255), and the phase rows show plan and actual percentages ten times too small (for example mobilisation 10% and construction 6.2% planned). The totals (67.18% planned, 55.39% actual) are consistent; this report uses the phase values multiplied by ten.
  • Basis for this week's change: the report's own weekly columns give +4.53% earned against +3.19% planned, but its "last week" planned value leaves out the 580.9 man-hours of testing and commissioning planned on 16-Nov. Against the 16-Nov-2026 report (260,522.6 planned, 206,635.3 earned man-hours) the change is +4.53% against +3.05% planned, which is used here.
  • The Physical-Chart Data sheet now gives the October achieved value as 49.2% (a round 20,000 effort units), against the 44.6% reported on 26-Oct-2026; the S-curve keeps 44.6%. The November value (55.39%) is now correct.
  • Forecast finish: the report summary and General Information sheet give 10-May-2027 (−105 days), matching P6, but the Milestones sheet and the milestone panel of the summary still give 08-Jun-2027 (−134 days). Testing and commissioning is 24-Dec-2026 in the Milestones sheet and 16-Mar-2027 in P6 and the Testing sheet. Levelling works are complete on 13-Oct-2026 in the Milestones sheet but open in P6, forecast 24-Nov-2026.
  • The works-done files 15 and 16 repeat last week's list of works unchanged, and file 16 still carries another project's header data (central sector, project manager Abdullah Al-Shunaifi, contractor Al-Injaz, dates of 24-Nov-2025 to 23-May-2026). Files 12, 15 and 16, the Look Ahead and Conclusion sheets and the Tracking Progress file label a cost-based progress figure as "actual"; this report uses physical progress (man-hour weighted) only.
  • The report week is the project week counted from site handover (26-Mar-2026 to 23-Nov-2026 is 242 days, week 34). The files carry the serial WPR-30 but state no week number.
  • Procurement Log: LV panel boards show 6 delivered against a total of 3; the tartan floor is marked not approved but 608 of 608 m² delivered. The new summary file 12 gives interlock 2,000 of 8,044 m² and curbs 5,000 of 8,900 delivered, against 5,173 of 8,173 m² and 8,868 of 8,868 LM in the log.
  • Safety figures disagree: the report summary gives 132,050 cumulative and 6,480 man-hours for the week (the 26-Oct values); the HSE statistics sheet gives 160,380 and 4,620 for 17–23 Nov-2026. Equipment on site is 17, 20 or 10 depending on the table.
  • Quality counts do not add up: NCRs 35 issued, 34 closed, 0 pending; MIRs 131 issued, 128 closed, 2 pending; FIRs 914 issued, 851 closed, 59 pending.
  • The Major Quantity Trackers block of the summary sheet still has its labels shifted by one row; this report uses the Major Quantities sheet. The report counts 165 critical activities against 164 open activities with negative float in the XER; the Failed Start List header is still dated 05-Oct-2026.
  • Still uncorrected from earlier reports: the Milestones sheet's baseline dates for programme approval (02-Jun-2026), mobilisation (25-Jan-2027) and testing and commissioning (29-Apr-2026); the Conclusion sheet's project end of 25-Jan-2026; the Issues sheet's MV cable entry marked completed while described as open.
